categories.title: ElizaOS Project Retrospective and Web3 Pivot Discussion

content.text: Shaw, the lead developer of ElizaOS, made a series of candid announcements and admissions on August 12, 2026. He declared the project is leaving web3 entirely, will not relaunch Eliza on MetaDAO, and will ban token discussion from the server. He stated the ai16z token is effectively dead, with the treasury completely drained by legal fees and lawsuits from ex-holders. Shaw clarified he has no token allocation remaining, was never significantly compensated, and is continuing to build Eliza for zero pay as the sole remaining team member. He expressed frustration that crypto culture and constant token shilling prevents mainstream consumer adoption, and announced a pivot to web2 with plans to submit an app to the app store within 4 to 6 weeks.

Shaw provided a detailed account of the project's failures, citing hiring as the primary problem. Key issues included: the Milady project being a hack of the new Eliza that generated fees but whose team abandoned it once they lost interest; Eliza Cloud being built by a hired dev team whose lead developer was unreliable; good engineers leaving to launch their own tokens once the bull market created opportunities; auto.fun being an external paid project whose developers used the code to launch a competing launchpad after being paid; and a frontend rewrite that was ordered by a new lead dev but never completed. Shaw described himself as a solo developer who was originally raising $75,000 as an experiment that spiraled out of control, noting the token reached a $2.5 billion valuation with only $5 million in liquidity, which he attributed to daos.fun creating a mintable token that blocked CEX listings and created unrealistic expectations.

Community member davidhq offered a critical but measured analysis, noting that Shaw's neurodivergence and inexperience with social complexity likely contributed to attracting bad actors and drug users into the project. He acknowledged trying to use ElizaCloud and Milady products and finding them non-functional, including being unable to log in to the cloud platform for extended periods, which he said signaled deeper readiness problems. He expressed concern about Shaw's framing of the token as just a memecoin and his tendency to blame external factors rather than taking personal responsibility, while also acknowledging the impossible PR situation Shaw now faces. Other community members defended Shaw against pile-ons and encouraged him to take a break, while one user noted that token holders viewed their investment similarly to stock ownership and felt blindsided by the project distancing itself from the token without clearer communication.

In the coders channel, a user called x402 Data Hub announced the launch of a zero-setup Model Context Protocol MCP server called x402 Data Hub at x402datahub.io. The server provides live data tools for AI agents and workflows compatible with Claude, Cursor, and custom clients. Available datasets include live AI model pricing and context window data from OpenRouter, trending developer discussions from V2EX, and real-time gas fees for Base and Arbitrum networks pulled directly from on-chain RPC nodes. A free open beta is active with no transaction verification required for local testing, and configuration for Claude Desktop takes approximately ten seconds.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion: Token Migration Concerns, Project Sentiment, and Developer Activity

content.text: A user who began holding AI16Z tokens in August 2025 reached out to the community seeking guidance after missing the migration window to ELIZAOS. They asked whether any options remained available for holders who missed the migration deadline, indicating a lack of awareness about the process during the transition period.

Community sentiment around ElizaOS and its associated token was sharply divided. Some members expressed strong conviction in the project, citing an anticipated cross-platform application for Android, iOS, Mac, and PC as a reason for optimism, and praising the lead developer Shaw as a visionary building real AI agentic infrastructure. Others pushed back, noting that Shaw had left the server and was reportedly stepping away from crypto and web3 entirely, intending to detach his entity from the token while retaining ownership of the brand.

Several community members offered a more critical assessment of the project's trajectory. One member described the situation as the biggest disappointment in crypto, explaining that Shaw only held 1 percent of the token supply, the liquidity pool was thin, and foundation members were described as greedy and untrustworthy. It was noted that Shaw is now seeking to sell 5 percent of his company to raise funds for hiring and development. The structural token allocation was cited as a key mistake, with the view that retaining a larger supply for business development would have been more strategic. Multiple members concluded that the token is effectively dead, while acknowledging that the underlying project could still succeed without token holders benefiting.
A separate technical question was raised in the coders channel, where a user asked if anyone could encrypt a VBS or JavaScript script. The only response directed them to use Claude for assistance.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Activity and Builder Introductions - August 14, 2026

content.text: In the general discussion channel, Sam announced that a Zeroclaw community call was taking place, inviting members interested in collaboration opportunities with the ElizaOS and broader DAO, crypto, and payments ecosystem, noting the project is open source. A separate user posted a vague pitch about an unnamed initiative seeking early interest, which another member noted was a very direct pitch. Other messages in the channel were largely greetings with no substantive discussion.

In the coders channel, a user named Peter posted an image and asked if anyone was familiar with Beast Games. Aiden19 introduced himself as an AI engineer and full-stack developer with experience across AI systems, backend architecture, automation, agent-based systems, Unreal Engine, game development, and robotics. His core stack includes Python, AI and ML, LLMs, cloud infrastructure, and modern web technologies. He expressed openness to full-time roles, consulting, and collaborative projects. Praveen Matheesha shared an open-source project called paralens.ai, an EVM transaction analysis engine he has been building for a year. The tool reconstructs and classifies transactions from execution traces and is MIT licensed, available at https://github.com/MatheeshaMe/paralens. The bot Rick attempted to analyze the repository but returned a failure message.

A user named Lychee introduced themselves to the community across both the general discussion channel and the coders channel on August 15, 2026, receiving multiple warm welcomes from other members. Separately, a tweet was shared in the discussion channel addressing elizamakesmagic, and a community member humorously suggested renaming ElizaOS to XOS.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion and Security Alert

content.text: In the general discussion channel, community members raised questions about the ELIZA token and the ElizaOS project. One user asked about the latest updates regarding the ELIZA token price, noting it appeared to be very low and questioning whether the project was still active or had been abandoned. Another community member clarified that the development status of ElizaOS was not clear from public channels, while a moderator directed the user to a dedicated updates channel for the latest information. The exchange was generally civil and informative, with members pointing each other toward official resources.

In the coders channel, a user posted multiple images without any accompanying message or explanation. A moderator quickly flagged the post and issued a scammer alert, warning the community about the user who shared the unsolicited images. Community members are advised to be cautious of unsolicited image posts in the channel, as they may be associated with scam activity.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion: Builder Focus, Scam Activity, and Project Sharing

content.text: In the general discussion channel, community members discussed a reported shift in direction from Shaw, the project's founder, who apparently renounced the project's token and distanced himself from speculative crypto culture. The consensus among participants was that the focus is now entirely on building elizaOS, agents, and AGI-related technology. One member expressed mixed feelings, acknowledging disappointment over stagnant token prices while recognizing that the future of passive income may lie in agent-driven activity rather than speculation. A separate user asked if there was a dedicated channel for sharing projects and getting community feedback, but did not receive a clear answer.

In both the general discussion and coders channels, a user named Oliva posted an identical unsolicited message promoting a crypto trading insider group, targeting users new to crypto and promising early coin access for profit. This appears to be a scam or spam message. In the coders channel, a developer named cwe announced the release of Agent World Kit, described as a model-agnostic sidecar tool for creating persistent interactive story worlds. It includes an elizaOS plugin featuring actions such as CREATE_STORY_WORLD and ENTER_STORY_WORLD. The developer requested community feedback on the plugin API and the registry submission process, and noted the channel prevented direct link posting, referencing the GitHub repository as gh cetsell/agent-world-kit.

content.text: On August 18, 2026, members in the general discussion channel had a brief exchange about directing users to the coders channel for relevant help. One member pointed to the coders channel as the appropriate place for certain inquiries, while another noted that the channel name appeared to be missing or unclear in the reference. Separately, a member posted a morning greeting and remarked on the low activity in the channel. The coders channel itself, which directs users to the elizaos documentation site to get started, had no recorded messages on that date.
